title: Cayetano clarifies P170K debt contribution proposal for richest Filipinos
summary: Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano clarified on Friday that his suggestion for contributions of P170,000 each from Filipinos to pay the country"s foreign debt was primarily directed to the…

blocks.text: Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano clarified on Friday that his suggestion for contributions of P170,000 each from Filipinos to pay the country’s foreign debt was primarily directed to the richest of the rich, adding that it was only voluntary.

During the presentation of the Department of National Defense’s (DND) budget at the Senate’s plenary session, Cayetano ended his line of questioning to budget sponsor Senator JV Ejercito by addressing the controversy.
Cayetano expressed his frustration, saying that his suggestion was twisted by people who had a grudge against him.

“What I actually said, if those who are able, the richest in the Philippines and the most generous, want to pay their P170,000, wouldn’t it be helpful?” Cayetano said in a mix of English and Filipino.
The minority senator said that he had done some computing and estimated that if the top 1% of the Philippines paid their share of P170,000, it would already result in P200 billion.
Cayetano said that he had also watched news anchors making comments about the suggestion, saying that they should be unbiased and well-researched.

“Ang sabi nila, ‘mahirap na buhay, sakto kang sweldo, bakit sila magbibigay?’. Ang magbibigay yung richest of the rich na gusto, kusa, at generous,” Cayetano said. (They said, ‘Life is hard, the salary is just enough; why would they give?' The ones who would give are the richest of the rich, willful, and generous.)
Cayetano also responded to calls saying that he should contribute first, saying that he has already offered. –NB, GMA News
